title: Eval witness fencing and automatic revert for staged model flips
creator: Aisha Malik
description: Motivation: current staged rollouts rely on aggregate score deltas computed from golden prompt pools. We frequently see noisy signals from distributional shifts (tokenization changes, context trimming) that cause spurious canary flips or slow unsafe rollbacks. This ticket implements an "eval witness fencing" abstraction: a small, stable set of deterministic witness prompts per customer-segment plus a lightweight statistical fence (hysteresis + persistence) to avoid oscillation. When the fence is breached we trigger an automated revert path that is observable and reversible by platform ops. Goals: 1) reduce false-positive rollbacks and false-negative regressions 2) make automated reverts explainable (root causes, top contributing prompts) 3) provide per-canary-level tuning knobs (sensitivity, persistence window, quorum) that play nicely with A/B and shadow experiments.
acceptance_criteria: Server-side Eval Witness API that returns per-canary witness-set metrics within 200ms
Configurable fence params (sensitivity, persistence, quorum) exposed in rollout policy config and Redwood Console
Automated revert runbook implemented: on fence breach, canary weight drops to previous stable model and a rollback PR is opened with evidence
Post-mortem artifacts automatically generated: top 10 contributing prompts, diffed generation examples, token-latency breakdown
End-to-end integration tests covering: steady-state, transient spike (noise), real regression and arbitrated A/B conflict
No increase in 95th percentile API latency by >2% in integration cluster during smoke tests
progress_updates: 2025-02-14: Ticket created after on-call incident where canary flipped due to tokenizer config drift (INC-2025-02-12) - initial spec reviewed with PM and SRE
2025-02-18: Spike completed - prototyped witness-set extraction script and sketch of statistical fence (rolling-median with hysteresis). Results: reduced alert noise on historical traces by ~45%

technical_notes: Witness selection: use deterministic seeding to sample prompts by fingerprint => stable per-customer witness sets. Avoids drift due to random sampling in production

Fence algorithm: two-stage detector: (1) per-prompt z-score against rolling baseline, (2) quorum and persistence window (default quorum=0.25, window=30m). On breach, compute aggregated effect-size and trigger revert if > threshold

Evidence bundle: includes raw prompt, baseline response, canary response, improved/dropped tokens, generation probabilities (top-k), and token-level latency. Bundles stored in S3 with lifecycle 90 days

Rollout integration: rollout controller will query Eval Witness API every 60s; controller supports soft-fallback (reduce traffic by 50%) and hard-fallback (full revert) depending on configured severity
Performance: collector is async by default and writes to a bounded in-memory queue to avoid backpressure. If queue fills, we sample down to preserve tail-latency SLAs
Security: evidence bundles are encrypted with tenant KMS keys when customer is on Private plan
qa_plan: Unit tests for detector logic with synthetic drift/regen cases
Integration test that runs shadow traffic and injects controlled regressions to validate auto-revert behavior
Chaos test: simulate delayed metric delivery and ensure hysteresis prevents flapping
Manual runbook validation with SRE: trigger auto-revert in staging and confirm telemetry, console alerts, and PR generation
risks: If witness set seeds are too correlated across customers, we may see systemic blind spots — mitigate by deriving seeds from customer_id + model_version
Evidence storage may grow quickly with verbose bundles; ensure lifecycle policies and optional sampling
Auto-revert may conflict with manual A/B experiments if policies are not correctly scoped — require explicit opt-in for cross-segment reverts
Metric staleness (delayed logging) could cause late reverts; hysteresis and persistence windows must be conservative by default
